text: You are going to investigate what happens when two different solids, S and T, dissolve in water.
Read all the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to carry out two experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the appearance of solid U.

Add about half of solid U to about 5cm of distilled water in a test-tube. Stopper the test-tube and
shake it to dissolve solid U and form solution U.
Divide solution U into two equal portions in two test-tubes and carry out the following tests.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
To the first portion of solution U, add about 1cm of dilute hydrochloric acid.
Test the gas produced.
Record your observations.

Keep the second portion of solution U for the test in (g)(i).

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Carry out a flame test on solid U.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Identify solid U.

tests on solid W
Add about half of solid W to about 5cm of distilled water in a test-tube. Stopper the test-tube and
shake it to dissolve solid W and form solution W.
Divide solution W into two equal portions in two test-tubes and carry out the following tests.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
To the first portion of solution W, add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of
aqueous silver nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
To the second portion of solution W, add the second portion of solution U.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Now add an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid to the mixture from (g)(i).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text: What conclusions can you draw about solid W?

text: You are provided with two solid salts, U and W.
Carry out the following tests on solid U and solid W, recording all of your observations at each
stage.
